Account policy (admins, a Settings component of yours): keep closed envelopes (completed, voided, declined, expired) for N days, 30 to 9,999, counted from when they closed; off by default. A template can carry its own period. 2. Purge level, chosen in the policy: the documents (pages, signed PDF, attachments and stamp pictures of that envelope); or documents and typed values; or all that and the personal details in the record (names, addresses, phone numbers, internet addresses and browsers replaced by 'Removed on <date>'). 3. A queue: 14 days before an envelope goes, the sender and admins get one email with the list. On the envelope page 'Keep it' (with a reason, in the audit trail) and, for admins, 'Hold' (a legal hold on an envelope or a folder: never purged while held, reason and who set it recorded, lifted only by an admin). The timer purges what is due (cron.ts). 4. Purge one envelope now: the sender or an admin picks the level on a closed envelope; it waits 14 days, can be cancelled in that time, then cannot be undone. 5. A redacted audit trail keeps its chain values and marks each changed line, so the page says 'Some details were removed on <date>. The record can no longer be recomputed for those lines.' instead of 'Record was altered'. 6. What stays, said on the setting, in the email, on the envelope page and on /security/processing: the SHA-256 of the signed file, its envelope ID and day, so /verify can say 'completed here, deleted since' (as for deleted accounts); copies already emailed to people; backups until the operator's backup cycle ends (from DATA_BACKUPS); evidence packs and exports already downloaded. After a purge, recipients' links say the sender deleted it. 7. Every policy change, hold and purge goes to the security record once sec-log has landed. API: GET and PUT /account/retention, POST and DELETE /envelopes/:id/hold, POST /envelopes/:id/purge. Honest words: never 'deleted everywhere'. Goal: a public body can run the whole product itself, as one container, on any cloud, on its own servers or on a network with no internet, with nothing calling home and every outside service optional.

Read first: node_modules/next/dist/docs (AGENTS.md: this Next.js version differs from what you know), especially standalone output.

Build:
1. Dockerfile, multi-stage, on a pinned base image digest with Node 22 LTS. The build runs npm ci (fonts are built then by scripts/copy-assets.mjs, so the runtime needs no network), next build with NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 set in both build and runtime, and Next's standalone output if this version supports it, otherwise a pruned node_modules. Run as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem and one writable volume at DATA_DIR. Add a HEALTHCHECK against a new GET /api/health that answers 200 only when the database opens, DATA_DIR is writable, the file store is not stopped (fileStoreWarning) and the internal timer ticked within 30 minutes, and otherwise says which of these failed. It gives out nothing about tenants.
2. deploy/compose.yaml (the app, a volume, an env file) and a Helm chart deploy/helm/growsigning: replicas fixed at 1 with strategy Recreate (SQLite has one writer, so say why in values.yaml), a PVC, a Secret for APP_SECRET and FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, and a NetworkPolicy whose egress is denied by default, with a list to allow.
3. src/server/outbound.ts, installed from src/instrumentation.ts before anything else runs. On start, compute the outside hosts the configuration implies: the SMTP host, api.stripe.com when Stripe keys are set, Twilio or the SMS webhook host, Google or Microsoft when configured, and later the TSA, OCSP and AI hosts. Log that list once and show it on /security as 'This server connects to: ...', with what each is for. With SOVEREIGN_MODE=1, wrap globalThis.fetch so any host outside that list plus OUTBOUND_ALLOW (comma separated) is refused with an error naming the host and the setting. Check the SMTP host the same way at start. Webhook targets are tenant-chosen: in sovereign mode they must match WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HOSTS. Log a refused host once an hour, not per call.
4. Air-gapped use: document and test that the server starts and works with no network. Payments, Google, Microsoft and SMS stay off, mail goes through an internal relay or is recorded as 'Not emailed', and signing links come from the API (recipient-view) or 'I will send the link myself'. scripts/release-bundle.mjs writes a release bundle: the image tarball (docker save), the SBOM from G03, SHA256SUMS, and a detached signature with an offline key (minisign or cosign key mode, per the owner's decision). scripts/verify-bundle.mjs checks it before docker load and refuses a bundle that does not verify.
5. Backups: scripts/backup.mjs makes a consistent copy of sign.db while the server runs. Use node:sqlite's backup function if this Node version has it (check: it is newer than 22.13), otherwise VACUUM INTO. It copies DATA_DIR/blobs with a manifest of SHA-256 sums and never copies FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY or APP_SECRET; say where those must be kept instead. scripts/restore.mjs checks the manifest and refuses a partial backup.
6. Reproducible build notes for source escrow: the lockfile, the pinned base digest, and the exact commands, so an escrow agent can rebuild the same image.
7. README section 'Running it yourself': one container, the volume, the settings that matter, what each outside service does and that each is optional, what works with no network, backups and restore, and why there is one replica. No claim of 'air-gap certified'. Say exactly what was tested ('started and completed an envelope with docker run --network none on <date>').

Tests (tests/sovereign.test.ts, no network): the computed host list for several configurations; sovereign mode refuses an unlisted host and allows a listed one; a webhook to an unlisted host is refused at save and at delivery; /api/health in each failure state; backup then restore gives a byte-identical database and blobs; a backup without its manifest is refused. Add scripts/container-smoke.sh, run by hand where Docker exists: build, run with --network none, create an envelope through the API, sign it through recipient-view, download the signed PDF, and check /verify matches.

Settings: SOVEREIGN_MODE, OUTBOUND_ALLOW, WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HOSTS. Add them to .env.example and the README table.

Leave out: Postgres and more than one replica (G26), HSM (G21), timestamping (G05).
A critic's concern about G02, which you must address: (1) Wrapping globalThis.fetch is not an egress control. nodemailer opens raw net/tls sockets (src/server/mail.ts), webhooks use node:http, node:https and node:net directly (src/server/webhooks.ts), and src/server/paydns.ts uses node:dns and node:net. So '/security: This server connects to: ...', worked out from the configuration, claims more than the code enforces. (2) Node 22 reaches end of life on 30 April 2027, and node:sqlite still prints an ExperimentalWarning on it, so a government image pinned to Node 22 is out of support within months. (3) A read-only root filesystem breaks Next.js's cache writes. (4) A container image distributed commercially in the EU falls under the Cyber Resilience Act. Enforce egress in the NetworkPolicy or firewall. On /security, say 'configured to connect to' and 'allowed by the network' as two separate facts. Keep the fetch wrapper as defence in depth and also hook net.connect and tls.connect. Base the image on the current Node LTS (24 or 26) and decide between node:sqlite and a stable driver. Mount a writable emptyDir for the Next cache. Add a CRA vulnerability-handling section.

simplify-start.brief:
This is a SIMPLIFY batch: you make what already exists simpler, you add no feature. The owner said: "make sure it's always user friendly and as simple and easy as possible to use". A UX researcher measured today's product (research/ux.json key "ux:baseline": counts per flow, every problem with its screenshot under tests/out/ux-baseline/, and the inventory of every setting) and a designer wrote research/ux-charter.md, which an independent designer then corrected (research/ux.json key "ux:check": corrections and merges; where the check and the charter disagree, the check wins). Read all three first. Measure with node tests/ux/flows.cjs <url> <folder> before and after (start your own dev server), and write the new counts for the flows you touched into your report: they become the ceilings for everyone after you. Keep every behaviour and rule the product has (the tests pin many of them; change a test only when the words or the layout it pins changed on purpose, and say so). Nothing a person could do before may become impossible: it may move behind More, never vanish. Phone 390x844 and 320x568 first, then desktop; screenshot before and after and look at them.
Your part: the way in, and the app's home and navigation. Files you will mostly touch: src/components/AuthForm.tsx, the confirm-email routes in src/server/routes-account.ts (or wherever confirmation lives), src/components/AppShell.tsx, src/app/app/page.tsx (Home), the confirmation email text in src/server/mail.ts or its template.
The designer's quick wins for this part, to do:
- Confirm the email address without leaving the tab: a 6-digit code typed in the same tab, the sign-up tab drops the banner by itself, and the email is 50 words or fewer.
- One start button: remove 'Send for signature', 'Send your first envelope' and 'Sign a document yourself' from Home; keep the sidebar's 'Send a document'; Home gets 'Recently completed' with Download on each row.
- Sidebar from 14 entries to 9: Envelopes becomes Documents, Inbox becomes To sign; Bulk send, PowerForms, Click-to-agree, Reports and Our impact go into a closed More group; 'Ask for help' and 'Help' become one Help; no '...' while the Paper saved card loads.
- Title-case the document name from the file name ('planting-partnership' becomes 'Planting partnership') so subject, lists and downloads read well.
The independent designer's corrections that apply here (they win):
- [longer flow] Quick win 2, signing your own document: Quick win 2 removes 'Sign a document yourself'. Today that is /app/envelopes/new?self=1, which prefills you as the signer. After the change, self-signing becomes: upload, Add me, step 2, step 3, Send, then find the signing page. That is a common job made longer, and no flow measures it. FIX: When the only person is the sender, step 3's main button reads 'Sign now' and opens the signing page in the same tab, with no invitation email. Add flow h-sign-myself, with today's ?self=1 path as its ceiling.
- [untestable] P5 vs Settings cards and the sidebar: 'Each card saves on its own with its button' puts several filled buttons on one Settings page. The sidebar's yellow 'Send a document' is also a primary button on every app page. P5's test ('exactly one') fails everywhere. FIX: Switches and selects save as soon as they change, with 'Saved' next to them. Text cards get a secondary Save. P5 counts only the page body and dialogs. Give the sidebar start button its own class and leave it out of the count.
- [untestable] P4 vs the charter's own screens: The envelope page has 5 folded sections, step 3 has '2 more things to check', step 2 has 'More fields', and Settings cards have their own More options. P4 says nothing else expands options, so its test fails on screens the charter itself designs. 'Remembered closed' can be read two ways. FIX: Define three kinds, each with a data attribute: data-more='screen' (at most 1 per screen), data-more='item' (at most 1 per item: person, file, field, card, row) and data-fold (content sections, closed by default, allowed). Count them by attribute. Replace 'remembered closed' with 'closed every time the screen opens'. The sidebar's More group is the exception: it opens by itself on a page inside it and remembers being open for that person, so daily Send to many users do not pay an extra click.
- [untestable] Consent word cap with the account's own text (P7, ds-consent-own): Account text of 60 words or fewer is shown inline. Together with our sentence and any line about the document, that can push the consent screen past 120 words. P6's 'sender's daily path' is also undefined. FIX: The 120-word cap holds with every option on. Show the account's text inline only while the total stays at or under 120; otherwise put it behind 'Read <Org>'s terms'. Define the daily path as: sidebar, Home, Documents, editor steps 1 to 3, the envelope page, Templates and emails to senders.
- [default] Key dates switches on with AI reading (ds-ai-repo): An admin who turns on 'Let the AI read document text' to get field suggestions also sends every completed contract to the AI and adds a new sidebar entry, without being told. FIX: The AI card says in one line what the switch is used for. Key dates gets its own switch. It reads only documents completed after it was turned on, unless the admin presses 'Look through older documents'.
- [default] Leaked-password check vs sovereign mode (ds-sec-policy, gov-G02): The check is on by default, but sovereign mode turns outside services off. A check that calls out either breaks sign-up or silently does nothing. FIX: In sovereign mode, use a bundled list or skip the check, and say so on /app/operator ('Leaked-password check off: no outside calls'). Never block sign-up because the check cannot run.
The researcher's problems that this part must solve:
- [high] The envelope page right after the first send is crowded: 37 choices, 436 words, 1.9 screenfuls. The header has Preview PDF, Download evidence pack, Clone, Save as template and Void. The person's card has 6 more buttons (Nudge, Copy link, Show QR code, Share on WhatsApp, Share by text message, Correct). These repeat 'Send reminder' and 'Edit envelope' a few lines above. A comment box with a 'Who can read it' select is always open. The audit trail shows the IP 127.0.0.1 and hash ids. The 'Sent' toast covers the person's action buttons, and the sidebar still says 0 sheets saved. (screenshot tests/out/ux-baseline/a-send-first/13-envelope-page-just-sent-full.png)
- [medium] The app home has 4 buttons that start nearly the same thing: the yellow 'New envelope', 'Send for signature', 'Send your first envelope' and 'Sign a document yourself'. The sidebar has 14 entries with jargon (Envelopes, Bulk send, PowerForms, Click-to-agree, Our impact), plus both 'Ask for help' and 'Help'. While loading, the Paper saved card shows '...' and 'sheets, or ... of a tree'. (screenshot tests/out/ux-baseline/a-send-first/06-app-home.png)
THE OWNER ADDED ON 2026-11-21 (this wins over anything above about hiding paper figures): "It's good to let people know how much they're saving for this individual sign but not the total since ours is tiny." So: the saving of ONE document stays and is shown where a person sends or finishes it (the review step's box 'Sending this digitally saves about 15 sheets of paper', the sent page, the signer's done screen): sheets, litres of water and CO2e, labelled as estimates with the link to the sources; leave out the fraction of a tree ('0.0018 of a tree') because a tiny fraction reads badly. What is hidden is every TOTAL (the account's 'Paper saved' card and sidebar counter, the public counters on the home and impact pages) until it is large enough to mean something (1,000 sheets; 10 trees planted).

Testable cap: at most 8 options with everything set up.

FIX: The main button names who it reminds ('Remind Ana Silva'). A per-person Remind appears only when 2 or more people are waiting at the same time.

If it is not, the email (sent before any browser is known) can be in one language and the page in another. Also, ds-lang-core's first sight shows the admin a select, while its Never forbids a select with one option.
